desc:
Given a string s of English letters (upper and lower case), reverse the order of its vowels and leave every other character where it is. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u in both lower and upper case. Characters keep their case; only the positions of the vowels are swapped among themselves.

For example, "hello" becomes "holle", and "Education" becomes "odicatuEn" (the vowels E u a i o are rewritten as o i a u E).
constraints: s consists of upper and lower case English letters
hints: Collect the vowels, reverse that list, and write them back. That works with O(n) extra memory. Can you swap in place?
Use one pointer from each end. Move the left one right until it sits on a vowel, and the right one left until it sits on a vowel.
Swap the two vowels, move both pointers one step inward and continue until the pointers meet.
editorial: Keep a pointer i at the start and j at the end of a character array. Advance i while it is not on a vowel and retreat j while it is not on a vowel. If i < j, swap the two characters and move both pointers. When they meet, every vowel pair has been swapped, which is exactly the reversal of the vowel sequence.

Each position is visited at most once, so the time is O(n); the array copy of the string uses O(n) space, which is unavoidable if strings are immutable. Remember to treat upper-case vowels as vowels as well.
